reason: D0 mainly provides a clamp/reference from net32 to VDD for the Q1 branch; if net32 is not used elsewhere and the branch is only for bias shaping, removing D0 typically preserves the core differential PMOS/NMOS switching around net3/net6. Caveat: if this diode sets a critical bias ceiling or provides startup clamping, removing it can shift IB1-related bias and affect operating point under some conditions.
impact_estimate: Low to Medium (bias/reference behavior may shift, core function remains).

reason: D1 is the symmetric clamp/reference for the Q2 branch (net29→VDD) and often serves the same protective/bias-limiting role rather than the main signal path. Caveat: removing it can change the IB3-related bias limit and transient recovery if net29 would otherwise swing excessively.
impact_estimate: Low to Medium (mainly affects bias limiting and robustness).

reason: R1 provides a resistive pull-down/bleeder on net26 (the Q3/Q2 branch node), which is typically used to stabilize bias or discharge the node; the main differential core (M2-M5 with M0/M1) can still operate without this bleed if net26 is otherwise defined. Caveat: net26 may float more during startup or transitions, potentially causing slower settling or extra offset in the bias branch.
impact_estimate: Low if net26 is otherwise well-defined; Medium if the bias branch relies on the bleed for stable startup/settling.
